'''Desmon Kenyatta Farmer''' (born October 7, 1981) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played briefly in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), for the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] and the [[San Antonio Spurs]].

==College career==
Farmer attended and played [[college basketball|collegiately]] for the [[University of Southern California]] (USC); he averaged 19 points per game and nearly five [[Rebound (basketball)|rebound]]s in his final two years combined, graduating in 2004.

==Professional career==
After being signed and eventually cut before the season started by the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]'s [[Indiana Pacers]] in 2004, Farmer played professionally in [[Greece]], [[Belgium]] and [[Poland]] before returning to the U.S. to play for the [[NBA Development League]]'s [[Tulsa 66ers]] in 2005–06, averaging 16.4 points per game.<ref>{{cite web|last=Evans |first=Jayda |url=http://seattletimes.nwsource.com/html/sports/2003311537_soni19.html |title=Farmer plants seed with Sonics |publisher=Seattletimes.nwsource.com |date=October 19, 2006 |accessdate=December 16, 2011}}</ref> Farmer was signed to a contract by the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] in October 2006, being waived on January 4, 2007,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sonics/news/waivers070104.html |title=Sonics Waive Farmer and Glyniadakis |work=Nba.com |date= |accessdate=December 16, 2011}}</ref> appearing in eight games during [[2006–07 NBA season|the season]].

After two seasons, with the 66ers and [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]]—also from the D-League—and a couple of months in [[Puerto Rico]], with [[Atléticos de San Germán]], Farmer was signed by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] on September 18, 2008.<ref>{{cite web |author=Spurs sign Vipers' Desmon Farmer by Clay Williams |url=http://www.kgbt4.com/sports/sports_story.aspx?id=193497 |title=Spurs sign Vipers' Desmon Farmer |publisher=Kgbt4.com |date=September 18, 2008 |accessdate=December 16, 2011 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130127021035/http://www.kgbt4.com/sports/sports_story.aspx?id=193497 |archive-date=January 27, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> After playing sparingly, he was waived on November 16, in order to make roster space available for another guard, [[Blake Ahearn]]; he signed with the [[Reno Bighorns]] in November 2009,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs_sign_blake_ahearn_081116.html |title=Spurs Sign Blake Ahearn |work=Nba.com |date= |accessdate=December 16, 2011}}</ref> after a brief passage in [[Croatia]] with [[KK Zadar]].<ref>[http://www.talkbasket.net/news/zadar-inks-desmon-farmer.html Zadar inks Desmon Farmer] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090215222915/http://www.talkbasket.net/news/zadar-inks-desmon-farmer.html |date=February 15, 2009 }}</ref>

On October 1, 2010, Farmer signed with [[Ironi Ashkelon]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Israel/basketball.aspx?NewsID=204716 |title=Israeli Basketball, Teams, Scores, Stats, News, Standings |publisher=Eurobasket |date= |accessdate=December 16, 2011}}</ref>

On January 31, 2013, he rejoined the [[Reno Bighorns]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/reno/bighorns_acquire_desmon_farmer_2013_01_31.html |title=BIGHORNS ACQUIRE DESMON FARMER |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2013-02-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160118101922/http://www.nba.com/dleague/reno/bighorns_acquire_desmon_farmer_2013_01_31.html |archive-date=2016-01-18 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On January 2, 2015, he signed with [[Sigal Prishtina]] of Kosovo.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/other-leagues/147183/desmon-farmer-signs-in-kosovo-with-sigal-prishtina.html Desmon Farmer signs in Kosovo with Sigal Prishtina]</ref>
